reason: Conversation 1 asked the sensible questions (flash pattern/code, stage of stall, restart behaviour, full model number), gave an unplug-first safety note, respected the 'no panels' boundary by offering only a filter-opening pump check, and ended by recommending an engineer with a useful fault summary while keeping pump and motor both in play. Its weakness is over-weighting carbon brushes and never mentioning a control board fault, but it never told her to buy a part. Conversation 2 never asked about the flashing light or code, asked her to remove the kickplate, suffered a service outage, repeated the hose check after she had already answered it, and then declared it 'highly likely' the drain pump motor was failing and advised an engineer to replace that specific part, which the ground truth marks as unsupported given the genuine uncertainty between pressure system, pump and board.
